oewn-01192356-v.learner: to not eat or drink certain foods or drinks.
examples: She avoids coffee and sweets while she is training.

oewn-02483482-v.learner: to say that something is not valid and has no force.
examples: The court avoided the contract because one side had lied.

oewn-03900459-n.learner: a small gift given to a guest at a party to keep as a reminder of it.
examples: Each child went home with a bag of party favours.
something has occurred of a most unexpected and serious nature
How wonderfully these sort of things occur!

oewn-00725311-v.learner: to come into your mind as a thought or idea.
examples: I am glad it occurred to me to mention it
though it had not occurred to me before.

oewn-02618403-v.learner: to be found to exist or be present somewhere.
examples: Gold occurs in small amounts in these hills.
The officer required the soldiers to lay down their guns.

oewn-00804290-n.learner: a risk in which there is danger.
examples: You take a chance when you swim alone in rough sea.

oewn-05098974-n.learner: a measure of how likely it is that something will happen; a number comparing the ways it can go well with all the ways it can go.
examples: The chance of rolling a six with one dice is one in six.

oewn-04609402-n.learner: a place where people do their work.
examples: She was still at work when I phoned the house.

oewn-03846937-n.learner: everything a writer or artist has made, or a large part of it.
examples: Her work as a painter changed a great deal over forty years.

oewn-05763880-n.learner: using your mind to learn and understand a subject, often by reading.
examples: After a year of hard work at her books, she understood chemistry well.

oewn-11473837-n.learner: in physics, the energy passed from one thing to another when a force moves an object, equal to the force times the distance moved in the direction of the force.
examples: In physics, work equals force times distance.

oewn-01723161-v.learner: to play a particular role or part.
examples: The part which I acted is now to be explained.

oewn-00013608-v.learner: to pretend to have a certain quality or feeling.
examples: She acted surprised when they gave her the gift, though she had known for weeks.

oewn-02531113-v.learner: to have an effect or result, often the one that was wanted or expected.
examples: The medicine acted quickly, and the pain was soon gone.

oewn-01098310-v.learner: to carry out the duties of your job or position.
examples: While the captain was ill, the first mate acted in his place.

oewn-01725433-v.learner: to behave in a way that is not natural, or in a false and showy way.
examples: Stop acting and just be yourself.

connotation.why: marks the behaviour as false rather than simply describing it

oewn-02750852-v.learner: to be good for performing on a stage.
examples: The play reads well, but it does not act well.

oewn-02394488-v.learner: to get in touch with someone.
examples: I finally connected with my old school friend by phone.

oewn-02394734-v.learner: to form a friendly understanding or relationship with someone.
examples: The new teacher connected with her students right away.

oewn-01071212-v.learner: to join people together so that they can talk to each other.
examples: The operator connected me to the hotel in Singapore.

oewn-01071413-v.learner: to join places or things by means of equipment for sending messages, such as phone lines.
examples: Phone lines now connect the villages in the valley.

oewn-01423776-v.learner: to put a plug into an electric socket.
examples: Connect the TV so we can watch the game tonight.

oewn-02753278-v.learner: to be timed so that one service follows on from another and travel can continue, as with trains or planes.
examples: The local train does not connect with the express, so you will have to wait.

oewn-01410222-v.learner: to hit or play a ball with success.
examples: He swung hard and connected, sending the ball over the fence.

oewn-01240325-v.learner: to land on something, or hit it firmly and fully.
examples: Her punch connected with his jaw.

oewn-02506927-v.learner: to put someone on trial, or to hear a case and sit as the judge at the trial.
examples: The same court judged both men in separate trials.

oewn-00674196-v.learner: to decide the result of a competition.
examples: Three cooks will judge the baking contest.

oewn-01893603-v.learner: to move back and forth, or to make something move back and forth.
examples: Shake the bottle well before you open it.

oewn-00014027-v.learner: to tremble, or to move as if trembling.
examples: His hands shook as he opened the letter.

oewn-01879288-v.learner: to move back and forth or from side to side.
examples: The little boat shook from side to side in the storm.

oewn-01765558-v.learner: to stir up the feelings or emotions of people, or disturb their peace.
examples: The news of the accident shook the whole town.

oewn-00560633-v.learner: to put someone or something into a certain state by shaking, or as if by shaking.
examples: She shook the sand out of her shoes.

oewn-01895631-v.learner: to shake or vibrate fast and hard.
examples: The old washing machine shook violently as it spun.
